reviews.quote: No professional review found for this line as of 2026-11; ratings inferred from specs and sibling-line reviews.

praises: 24GB DDR5-5600 is the most RAM of any laptop in this budget class — heavy tab/VM/app multitasking just works
Latest-gen Arrow Lake-U refresh runs cool and quiet with strong single-thread speed
1TB SSD plus 24GB makes a genuinely long-lived office workhorse
NPU is Copilot-ready for on-device AI features
complaints: $1,299.95 for a chassis that has a backlit option elsewhere but not here, and a probably-TN panel
USB-C is data-only yet again on HP's top budget trim — no PD, no DP
Intel Graphics 4Xe is weaker for games than the cheaper Ultra 5 125H's Arc iGPU
Same plasticky 15s shell and bloatware (Adobe offers, McAfee, OMEN hub leftovers) as the $850 SKU

standouts: 24GB DDR5 + 1TB: the highest RAM ceiling in the budget class for future-proof multitasking
dealbreakers: At $1,299.95 the data-only USB-C, likely-TN panel, and missing backlight are hard to accept — the $999.97 Ultra 5 125H config beats it in more ways than it loses
design_philosophy: The spec-sheet max of HP's budget 15: newest U-series silicon, an unusual 24GB single-DIMM, and 1TB — numbers that top every column — mounted in the same unchanged 15s plastic chassis with the same neutered USB-C and an unstated panel. It is the clearest example of this whole class's pattern: HP spends on what appears in the filter panel, not on what you touch and look at.
rating_notes: No pro review found (see SHARED-budget-misc.md). Platform-anchored on Core Ultra 7 255U (Arrow Lake-U refresh): efficient → battery 6.0 (best of HP group), NPU ~13 TOPS → ai_ml 2.5, 4Xe iGPU weaker than Arc 125H → gaming 2.2. 24GB RAM pushes productivity to 6.9. Panel unstated → assumed TN per BUDGET_LIST rule. BBY weight field (2.3 kg) is a carton error; real ~1.66 kg. Image URL best-guess BBY CDN pattern.
